quarterly_data.signal: Passive Components segment FY2026 (management's analysis): sales JPY 593,201 million, segment profit JPY 41,831 million, segment assets JPY 1,007,684 million (+6.2%). Capacitors (ceramic, aluminum electrolytic, film) sales JPY 257,472 million (+9.9%); inductive devices JPY 216,210 million (+5.8%); other passive components (RF components, piezoelectric material / circuit-protection components) JPY 119,518 million (-1.3%). Management states ceramic capacitors grew sales on automotive and industrial equipment demand but profit declined, partly on lower average selling prices; aluminum electrolytic and film capacitors grew sales on industrial equipment demand such as renewable energy and AI servers and raised profit despite JPY 2.8 billion of restructuring costs (mainly in the first half) under portfolio management; inductive devices grew sales on automotive and industrial demand with a slight profit decline on a worse product mix; RF components saw lower ICT and industrial sales but improved profitability; piezoelectric / circuit-protection components grew sales and profit on industrial demand. Segment business ROA (ROIC) 4.8% (prior year 3.3%).
quarterly_data.figure: Capacitors JPY 257,472 million (+9.9%); inductive devices JPY 216,210 million (+5.8%); ceramic capacitor profit down on lower ASPs

quarterly_data.signal: Other segments FY2026 (management's analysis): Sensor Application Products segment profit JPY 20,748 million (+316.4%) - TMR sensors grew on smartphones and automotive, and MEMS sensors (microphones for ICT, motion sensors for industrial equipment) turned from a loss to a profit; Magnetic Application Products segment profit JPY 26,951 million (+698.1%), segment assets JPY 613,605 million (+15.8%), with magnets growing on automotive and the loss narrowing; Energy Application Products segment profit JPY 246,682 million (+5.2%), segment assets JPY 2,686,182 million (+38.2%) - small smartphone batteries up on new-model effects, mid-sized batteries up on industrial demand, industrial power supplies recovering gradually; Other (mechatronics, smartphone camera-module microactuators) segment loss JPY 10,230 million. Segment business ROA (ROIC): sensors 4.7% (prior year 0.2%), magnetic 8.4% (1.0%), energy 25.7% (27.3%).

quarterly_data.signal: Management's analysis of the JPY 48.2 billion FY2026 operating-profit increase: higher sales volumes in all segments added JPY 128.6 billion, rationalization cost-downs JPY 18.8 billion and the effect of the prior year's restructuring JPY 5.9 billion, while selling-price reductions cut JPY 53.2 billion, SG&A rose JPY 44.6 billion (including higher R&D, centred on secondary batteries), lower one-time gains cut JPY 3.3 billion and the stronger yen JPY 10.6 billion (lower restructuring costs added JPY 6.6 billion). quarterly_data.signal: Mid-term plan (FY2025-FY2027) scorecard: FY2026 actual vs FY2027 target - net sales JPY 2,504.8 billion vs a JPY 2,500 billion target (about 5% annual growth; 10% or more is the medium-to-long-term aim after portfolio transformation); ROE 9.8% vs 10% or more; ROIC 7.5% (WACC 7.0%) vs 8% or more; operating margin 10.9% vs 11% or more; the target assumes JPY 135/US$ (FY2026 actual JPY 151/US$). Management states it defines the broad AI-related market (data centers and servers, edge AI devices, smart glasses, AI smartphones, humanoid robots, ADAS, semiconductor equipment) as the 'AI ecosystem market', most of whose businesses are already 'growth areas' in its portfolio management, and intends to invest more aggressively in them, also using a strategic-investment allocation.

quarterly_data.signal: R&D expenses FY2026 JPY 289,668 million (+14.2% YoY, 11.6% of sales). Themes the company states: next-generation MLCCs, inductors and EMC components (smaller, higher performance) and parts for higher-frequency modules; next-generation electronic components combining thin-film, materials and roll-to-roll technology; next-generation high-recording-density HDD heads; less rare-earth content in high-performance magnets; next-generation lithium battery materials and high-efficiency power supplies. A new business unit for smart-glasses solutions (gaze-intent detection algorithm and devices, ultra-compact high-resolution full-color laser module). Results this year: an ultra-compact spin photodetector using spintronics for high-speed light detection, operation demonstrated with Nihon University, expected to apply to photonics-electronics convergence devices for AI data centers and to smart glasses; an analog reservoir AI chip modelled on the cerebellum (fast, lightweight real-time learning) developed with Hokkaido University.
